answer: In the Experimental Economics (ee) replication project of the supplied dataset all 18 unique original studies were conducted offline (online.o == 0 in every row, no missing values); because the dataset has no native lab/field/online venue column, the 'lab setting' is operationalised as a proxy through the available online.o marker (lab := online.o == 0), giving a point estimate of 18/18 = 1.00 with a 95% Wilson interval of [0.824, 1.000] (width ≈ 0.176, reflecting the small n = 18 rather than genuine ambiguity in the data), while a stricter sensitivity proxy that further requires a student subject pool (lab := online.o == 0 ∧ subjects.o == 'students', in which case the single community-subject original by Charness and Dufwenberg 2011 is excluded) yields 17/18 ≈ 0.94 with a 95% Wilson interval of [0.742, 0.990] (width ≈ 0.248); the qualitative conclusion that essentially every original in the EE sample was carried out in a lab or lab-like offline setting is therefore robust to the proxy choice.

payload.workflow: 1) Load study_data and filter to project=='ee' → n=18 unique originals by id (no duplicates; project=='ee' ≡ discipline='Economics' verified). 2) Lock two 'lab setting' proxies on the .o side — primary A: online.o == 0; sensitivity B: online.o == 0 AND subjects.o == 'students'. 3) Deduplicate by id (trivial in ee: 18==18). 4) Compute fractions 18/18 and 17/18. 5) Compute 95% Wilson CIs (z=1.96): A → [0.8241, 1.0000], width 0.1759; B → [0.7424, 0.9901], width 0.2477. 6) Cross-check selection identity: 18 ee rows in study_data ↔ 18 'Experimental Economics' rows in success_data, all 18 matched by first-author surname + pub_year (sanity-check only, no setting columns in success_data). 7) Diagnostics within ee: online.o all 0; subjects.o 17 students + 1 community (ee.4 Charness); pub_year 2011=8, 2012=6, 2014=3, 2013=1; experiment_country.o US=11, Germany=2, Switzerland=2, UK=1, Australia=1, Austria=1; compensation.o all 'cash'; zero NaN in online.o and subjects.o → no imputation required.
